title: Inertia projections are locally of finite type
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal X/S$ be an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Its inertia $I_{\mathcal X/S}$ and projection $r:I_{\mathcal X/S}\to\mathcal X$ are those of [def-sfb-moduli-inertia]: objects are pairs $(x,\alpha)$ with $\alpha$ an automorphism of $x$, and $r$ forgets $\alpha$. Then $I_{\mathcal X/S}$ is an algebraic stack and $r$ is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] and locally of finite type. Here locally of finite type means that after every scheme base change $T\to\mathcal X$ and every etale scheme chart $V\to I_{\mathcal X/S}\times_{\mathcal X}T$, the composite $V\to T$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; the 2-fibre product is [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. No quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 050Q (lemma-inertia), absolute inertia and its representable locally finite type projection.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-inertia-second-diagonal-geometry] in its absolute case $\mathcal Y=S$. Its last sentence identifies the relative inertia with absolute inertia, with the same objects, arrows and forgetful projection as [def-sfb-moduli-inertia]. Its algebraicity and representability clauses therefore give that $I_{\mathcal X/S}$ is algebraic and $r$ is representable by algebraic spaces. No local finite type conclusion is taken from this node.

Fix $x:T\to\mathcal X$. Over $H\to T$, an object of $I_{\mathcal X/S}\times_{\mathcal X}T$ is $(y,\alpha,\beta:y\xrightarrow{\sim}x_H)$. Send it to $\beta\alpha\beta^{-1}\in\operatorname{Aut}(x_H)$. The inverse sends $\gamma$ to $(x_H,\gamma,1)$. An arrow to $(y\prime,\alpha\prime,\beta\prime)$ is an isomorphism $v$ satisfying $v\alpha=\alpha\prime v$ and $\beta\prime v=\beta$. It exists uniquely exactly when the two conjugated automorphisms agree: necessarily $v=(\beta\prime)^{-1}\beta$. Thus these functors are quasi-inverse; their comparison on an object is $\beta$. The formulas commute with pullback, including its canonical comparison isomorphisms. They give an equivalence over $T$ with the discrete sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X,T}(x,x)$, preserving the actual projection to $T$. This is a calculation with the inertia and 2-fibre-product definitions.

By [lem-sfb-stack-isom-space-locally-finite-type] with $a=b=x$, the sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X,T}(x,x)$ is an algebraic space locally of finite type over $T$. All its hypotheses hold: $T$ is an arbitrary $S$-scheme and $x$ an object of the given algebraic stack. Step 2 presents the scheme base change of $r$ by exactly this space over $T$. Hence, for every etale scheme chart $V$ of that base change, $V\to T$ is locally of finite type, by the chartwise conclusion of the cited node. Since $T\to\mathcal X$ was arbitrary, this is precisely the asserted local finite type of $r$. Neither the identification nor the Isom theorem requires quasi-compactness or a Noetherian hypothesis.
